newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE should change laws to lure investors - official.
newsitem.headline: UAE should change laws to lure investors - official.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates should change some of its laws to make the Gulf Arab state more attractive to foreign investors, an official said in remarks published on Saturday.
"I call for a change of some laws relating to investment," Dubai Economic Department general director Mohammad al-Abbar told Al-Khaleej newspaper.
"In Dubai and all of the emirates there is still the lack of a federal law to organise the investment process and enduce businessmen to come to the country," he said.

The UAE and other Gulf Arab states are moving too slowly to lure foreign and local investment and should overhaul regulations to boost investor confidence in their oil-rich economies, officials and financial experts say.

The Gulf economies are dominated by the government sector, and although Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, the UAE, Qatar and Oman all speak of a bigger private sector role, in many cases the privatisation wheels needed for diversification are dragging.

Experts say the huge family-owned companies which dominate the UAE economy are unwilling to give up market territory to foreign investors -- a trend that needs to be broken in order for the country to diversify its economy.
